answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, independently verified stake to an identity anchor before it can earn reputation or vote on payments. When a bridge of agents endorses a newcomer, their stakes remain exposed for a challenge period; proof that the newcomer is controlled by an existing operator lets challengers slash the endorsers and the new account. A Sybil attacker must therefore acquire and risk real capital for every identity, while coordinating a vine of fake accounts also multiplies the stake at risk.
